I like to butcher languages in my free time, so recently I've started messing around with Dutch. I wanted to see what it would sound like if it were Scandinavian, so I influenced it with Swedish to begin the mutation. I started this project today and so far I have a word-base of ~600 words; probably enough that I suppose I could show it off and receive criticism.

Let me tell you a story about my dog:

Min honda zijna van ên ouda verelda. E krijga et honda langa gelenda vên E zijna mâr ên kinda. E noijt vervachtat dat E zou hâlat ên huisdiera, mâr E doat. Et honda zijnat vôr verkôpa en E zijnat endast bezoeka vên et honda zittat pa min ronda. Het lijka dat et honda kiesat me.

English:

My dog was from an old world. I got the dog long ago when I was only a kid. I never expected that I would receive a dog, but I did. The dog was for sale and I was only visiting when the dog sat on my lap. It seems that the dog chose me.

Right now the language is nothing but a Nordlang creole, but I plan to distinguish it... somehow. I've considered adding Japanese vocabulary (mostly adjectives) to the language, because Swedish and Japanese seem to really go well together. Maybe once that is settled, I could consider playing around with the suffixes, roots, and prefixes from the three language and create new words.

Grammar and spelling is really experimental.

A brief rundown of the grammar displayed in the example:

Ik -> E. Kind of got the idea from Afrikaans that pronouns should be simplified, so in addition to E, there are Je (you), He (he), Se (she), Ve (we), Ze (they). The different forms of "you" was a nuisance and she/they (zij/ze) was bothersome. While you are not likely to spot the difference between a spoken Se and a spoken Ze, on paper it makes reading smoother.

Zijna: to be. This is the infinitive, imperative, and present indicative form of the word. The indicative present is Zijnat. Notice how like Swedish the verb does not change depending on the subject. So simple. To "create" the verbs, I use the present/imperative form of the verb and add -a. Most verbs are originally Dutch, only a few are Swedish in origin.

Een -> ên. The accent signifies that the long-vowel sound should be used. I'm just playing around with this for a bit. If it does stay, it would only be in use for professional writing (books, essays, websites).

I also added -a's to every noun. I do not know why.

The Team-Up System Revamp is now live!

Here's the highlights of what's available in the first batch of the Team-Up 2.0 revision updates:

Power Trees & Leveling

Team-Ups will now gain experience and levels, along with their own power points to spend on powers. This allows all sorts of new build options to open up - customize your Team-Up to play how you want it to play. A Team-Up gains a power point every Mastery Level.

For players that prefer to use their Team-Up in "away" mode, build options are available, and "away" powers are now highlighted in the Team-Up's power UI. Many of these powers also have power synergies with other powers in the tree, so there very well could be multiple "away" builds for a single Team-Up.

Team-Up Instant-XP will be delivered to all accounts via the in-game delivery system. These are a one-time use potion that will jump up the Team-Up's Mastery Level, to give existing Team-Up users a jumpstart into the new system. These provide a flat amount of XP, so they can either be used once per Team-Up to give everyone on your roster a boost, or you can use multiple potions on a single Team-Up to boost them into higher levels.

New Powers & Signature

Almost all Team-Ups have received some new powers as part of the update, and all Team-Ups now have a purple-marked Signature power at the bottom of their tree. This is identical to a player's signature - a powerful attack with a cooldown. It can be increased using power points just like a player's signature is able to.

Styles

At the top-right of the Team-Up UI, you'll be able to select the Style, identical to the former "Tier 1" passive selection. The options available are Bodyguard (permanent Team-Up), Assist (short-duration high-burst damage Team-Up), and a third option unique to the Team-Up that provides a boost to the player while they are away.

Items

New Team-Up items dropped in the world will look a bit different. The base affix pool has been significantly changed to allow for more impactful affixes, and have baseline stats that affect the Team-Up equally, ensuring that equipping items has a positive effect (similar to the defense rating on Slot 2-5 gear for players). Cosmic Team-Ups are also now able to be found in the world.

Team-Up Gear Boosts sold in the Team-Up Advance Packs are now being fulfilled as of this patch, to help you gear out every Team-Up in your roster quickly.

  • Week 2: Free Coupon for a the Hero of Your Choice (excluding Doom)
  • Week 3: Surprise Pet
  • Week 4: Surprise Team-Up
